mainTopic: The rules for how many witnesses each legal act needs and when they must be told 'כתובו'. Then רבא's question about קנין, and a dispute over when a מודעא may be written.
overview: This amud finishes a list of rules about witnesses. מחאה (a protest against someone holding your land) and מודעא (an advance declaration that a sale is forced) each need two witnesses, and the witnesses may write them down without being told to. הודאה (admitting a debt) needs two witnesses, but they may write a document only if the person tells them 'כתובו'. קנין needs two witnesses and no 'כתובו', and קיום שטרות (confirming documents) needs three. The גמרא gives the memory aid ממה״ק. רבא then asks: if קנין is like an act of בית דין it should need three people, and if it is not, it should need 'כתובו' like הודאה. He answers that קנין is not a court act, but a plain קנין is normally meant to be written down, so permission to write is assumed. The גמרא then turns to מודעא. רבה and רב יוסף allow one only against a person who ignores the court, while אביי and רבא allow it even against law-abiding people. The amud ends as the חכמי נהרדעא begin a general rule about every מודעא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Protest and advance declaration: two witnesses, no instruction to write needed
steps.stepSummary: The list ends the rule of מחאה (no 'כתובו' needed). It adds that a מודעא needs two witnesses, and they may write it down without being told to.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and he does not need to tell them 'Write.' A declaration that a sale is forced must be made before two witnesses, and he does not need to tell them 'Write.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of a list of rules. It finishes the rule for מחאה and gives the rule for מודעא: two witnesses, and no need to say 'כתובו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For both מחאה and מודעא, two witnesses are enough. The witnesses may put it in writing on their own, even if the person never told them to.

keyTerms.meaning: A protest by the owner that someone is holding his land without right
An advance declaration that a sale or gift he is about to make is being forced on him, so it will not count
In front of two witnesses
'Write!' An explicit instruction to the witnesses to write a document

phrases.english: and he does not need to say 'Write';
a declaration — in front of two,
and he does not need to say 'Write';

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of רב נחמן's rules (quoted by רבא) that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחאה and מודעא each need two witnesses, and the witnesses may write them down without being told 'כתובו'.

steps.title: Admission, acquisition, and confirming documents
steps.stepSummary: A הודאה needs two witnesses and an explicit 'כתובו'. A קנין needs two witnesses and no 'כתובו'. קיום שטרות needs three.
steps.simpleTranslation: An admission is made before two witnesses, and he must tell them 'Write.' An act of acquisition is made before two, and he does not need to say 'Write.' Confirming documents needs three.
steps.whatsHappening: The list goes on with three more acts. It says how many people each one needs and whether 'כתובו' is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הודאה is the one item in the list that needs 'כתובו'. A written record of the admission works against the person admitting, so witnesses may not write it on their own. קנין, like the earlier items, needs no such instruction. קיום שטרות stands apart: it needs three, because it is a court act.

keyTerms.meaning: An admission that one owes money
A formal act of acquisition, here done with a cloth or similar item
Confirming that the signatures on a document are real
With three people, the size of a בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: Two witnesses for מחאה, מודעא, הודאה and קנין. Only הודאה needs 'כתובו'. קיום שטרות needs three.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מוֹדָעָא (a declaration that a sale is forced) with הוֹדָאָה (admitting a debt). The words sound alike, but their rules about 'כתובו' are opposite.

phrases.english: an admission — in front of two,
and he needs to say 'Write';
an acquisition — in front of two,
and he does not need to say 'Write';
and confirming documents — with three;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the same list of rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הודאה needs two witnesses plus 'כתובו'. קנין needs two witnesses without 'כתובו'. קיום שטרות needs three.

steps.title: A memory aid for the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the letters ממה״ק to help remember the order of the rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to give a short memory aid, so the learner can keep the four items of the list in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter stands for the first letter of one item: מחאה, מודעא, הודאה, קנין. It adds no new law. It only helps you remember.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, often made of the first letters of the items

phrases.english: A memory aid: M-M-H-K.
phrases.notes: The letters stand for מחאה, מודעא, הודאה, קנין, in the order they were just listed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the list just given in a short memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four items are remembered as ממה״ק: מחאה, מודעא, הודאה, קנין.

steps.title: רבא's difficulty: what kind of act is a קנין?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks how to understand קנין. If it is like an act of בית דין, it should need three people. If it is not, it should need 'כתובו' like an admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If anything here is hard for me, this is. What is this acquisition like? If it is like a court act, it should need three. If it is not like a court act, why doesn't he need to say 'Write'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a challenge against one item in the list, the rule for קנין. He traps it between two options, and each option clashes with the rule as stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a court act explains why witnesses may write without being told. But a court needs three people, and קנין needs only two. If קנין is not a court act, it should be like הודאה, where 'כתובו' is required. Either way, part of the rule seems wrong.

keyTerms.term: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
keyTerms.meaning: 'If anything is hard for me, this is what is hard for me': a way of pointing to the weakest point
What is it like? How should we understand it?
An act done by a court
It should require three
Why?

steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides the legal nature of קנין: is it a court-type act, or a private act like an admission? The answer will settle how many people it needs and whether 'כתובו' is required.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי, הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי –
phrases.english: Rava said: If something is difficult for me, this is difficult for me —
this acquisition, what is it like?

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּמַעֲשֵׂה בֵּית דִּין דָּמֵי, לִיבְעֵי תְּלָתָא!
phrases.english: If it is like a court act, it should require three!

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא כְּמַעֲשֵׂה בֵּית דִּין דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: If it is not like a court act,
why does he not need to say 'Write'?
phrases.notes: He means it should then be like הודאה, which does need 'כתובו'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי, הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the rule about קנין from step 2 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that קנין needs only two witnesses and no 'כתובו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a two-sided trap. As a court act, קנין would need three people. As a non-court act, it would need 'כתובו' like הודאה. The stated rule fits neither option.

steps.title: רבא answers his own question about קנין
steps.stepSummary: רבא decides that a קנין is not like an act of בית דין. It needs no 'כתובו' because a plain קנין is normally meant to be written.
steps.simpleTranslation: After רבא asked the question, he answered it himself. Really, a קנין is not like an act of בית דין. So why don't the witnesses need to be told 'write'? Because a plain קנין is made with the plan of writing it down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question he asked in Step 4. He picks the second side, that a קנין is not like בית דין, and explains why no 'כתובו' is needed anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a קנין is not an act of בית דין, two witnesses are enough and three are not needed. The problem was that a הודאה, which is also not בית דין, does need 'כתובו'. רבא explains the difference: people who make a קנין usually want a document, so permission to write is assumed.

keyTerms.meaning: He answered it (solved the question)
Really, in truth (the real answer is...)
A plain קנין, made without saying anything special
Is meant to be written down

steps.whatToRemember: A קנין needs only two witnesses because it is not בית דין. It needs no 'כתובו' because a plain קנין is meant to be written.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the list in Step 2 treats קנין differently from both הודאה and קיום שטרות.

phrases.english: After he asked, he then answered it:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבא, who asked the question in Step 4.

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם לָאו כְּמַעֲשֵׂה בֵּית דִּין דָּמֵי;
phrases.english: Really, it is not like an act of the court;
and here, what is the reason
that he does not need to say "write" –
because a plain acquisition is meant to be written down.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the question and adds a new reason for the part that seemed hard
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a קנין is not like בית דין, it should need 'כתובו' just like a הודאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קנין is not like בית דין, so two witnesses are enough. It still needs no 'כתובו' because a plain קנין is meant to be written down.

steps.title: A מודעא only against someone who ignores the court
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף say a מודעא is written only when the other side will not obey בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: we write a מודעא only against a person who does not obey the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the rules of a מודעא. רבה and רב יוסף set a limit on when one may be written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מודעא lets a person cancel a sale he is being forced into. רבה and רב יוסף allow it only when the other side ignores בית דין. If the person would listen to the court, the seller should take him to court instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
We write
Does not obey the court's ruling

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both say:
We do not write a preemptive declaration,
phrases.notes: This is the advance declaration from Step 1, saying "I am only doing this because I am being forced."

phrases.english: except against someone who does not obey the court's ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of קנין and opens a new discussion about מודעא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מודעא may be written only against a person who will not obey בית דין.

steps.title: A מודעא even against law-abiding people
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא disagree with רבה and רב יוסף. They say a מודעא may be written even against people who do obey בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: we write a מודעא even against people like me and you.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא give the opposite view. They allow a מודעא even when the other person is honest and obeys the court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Me and you" stands for ordinary people who listen to בית דין. In their view, a מודעא is allowed even when going to court would also be possible. So they reject the limit that רבה and רב יוסף set in Step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
Against me and against you (ordinary law-abiding people)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two pairs of אמוראים here. רבה and רב יוסף limit the מודעא, and אביי and רבא allow it more widely. Don't mix the pairs up.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both say:
Even against me and against you.
phrases.notes: They mean even against people like us, who would obey the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבה and רב יוסף's limit from Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מודעא may be written even against a person who obeys בית דין.

steps.title: The חכמי נהרדעא begin a rule about every מודעא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמי נהרדעא start a new general rule about every מודעא. Their statement continues after this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמי נהרדעא say: every מודעא...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new statement from the חכמי נהרדעא. Only the opening words appear here, and the rest comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "every מודעא" show that a general rule for all such advance declarations is about to be stated. We have to wait for the next words to learn what that rule is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages of the city of נהרדעא
Every, any

phrases.english: The Sages of Neharde'a say:
Any preemptive declaration

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of מודעא with a new general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens a general rule about every מודעא (the rule itself is finished after this point).
